doc.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022

title: Folk music from other cultures
summary: She loves African and Scandinavian folk music and mentions Hardanger fiddle player Benedicte Maurseth.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I think of Sun Ra for some reason when you said that. Yeah. Are you affected by music from other cultures? Gamelan and so forth?

Yeah, yeah. Very much, very, very much, folk music from everywhere, especially Africa, all the different African countries. Amazing music. Amazing folk music from all over the world really. I also love Scandinavian folk music very much and I remember when I first listened to a recording I was expecting, I don’t know what I was expecting, some like jigs or waltzes or polkas or something. And it was this wild, very like keening across the mountain kind of thing. It sounded to me very much like some Irish folk music. And well there was a lot of interchange there with the Vikings you know. So they are actually

connected, they’re related. One of the people I met in recent years is a woman named Benedicte Maurseth. And she plays a Norwegian Hardanger fiddle which has extra strings so there’s a lot of resonance there. And she has done some very beautiful things. So I’ve been listening to her things and Elena Villamar is a Swedish singer who sings Swedish music and plays violin and is very intense. She grew up in the North of Sweden. Her grandmother saw little people there. Anyway —
